title: Choose model initialization, fallback, and a managed hook
summary: Supply known initial values in the model; use defaultValue for undefined data and return an Observable for lifecycle-managed side effects.

fact_links.support: Supports model initialization when the computed value is available before build.
Supports retaining supplied values and filling eligible undefined values.
Supports subscribing to the returned onInit Observable and disposing it when the field component is destroyed.
Explains why the illustration returns the stream rather than creating an unmanaged manual subscription.

conditions: Visible keyed inputs with initial data supplied before mount.
The hook stream remains open until the owning field component is destroyed.
limits: The hook records events only; it is not an asynchronous loading or initialization policy.
No guarantee about preset/defaultOptions precedence or arbitrary later model mutation is made.
Hide/show must not be equated with destruction of the outer field component.
prerequisites: Formly core and Material 6.3.12; candidate fixture pins Angular/Material 18.2.14.
Import ReactiveFormsModule, FormlyModule.forRoot(), and FormlyMaterialModule; mount the returned form/model/fields/options using formly-form.
Call the factory once per mounted form; these are original illustrations, not upstream example excerpts.
assertions: The supplied model value survives its configured fallback.
The undefined fallback value becomes Default for undefined.
The returned onInit stream records an event while mounted.
After component destruction, another event is not recorded.

verification.details: Original candidate illustration executed with pinned Angular JIT TestBed and Material in headless Chrome. All 17 bounded fixture assertions passed, including supplementary reset-on-hide and shared-key cases; TypeScript noEmit passed. This is not whole-library or cross-version qualification.
